why: cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_codemother.py fires its sealed messages over the REAL bus to the REAL codemother, so the clearance gate's refusals are raised inside the live device's process against the live world. Its fixture boats then appear in CairnCommons/troubles/ as genuine troubles: measured 2026-09-09, three files (boat-crossed-to-proved-uncovered-6acd0cf29fe1, -cfa17e00b0a7, and -an-intention-declares-its-gated-hands) whose evidence points at /tmp/cm_admit_*/a_fixture_component/proofs/test_fixture.py — scratch directories that no longer exist. They stand in the session-open banner as LIVE TROUBLE beside real ones. Law 7 cuts both ways: a record of truth may never collapse an error, and it may never be fed a manufactured one. The in-process half of the same leak was sealed the same day (test_clearance.py now gives its default ModuleRaiser a sandbox world via set_diagnostic_roots), but that patch cannot reach a raise that happens in ANOTHER process. Fixing this needs a way for a live device to know a message is fixture traffic, which is a design choice for Akien, not a patch.

occurrences.needs: a ruling on how a live device recognises fixture traffic
